requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP on lan-a and hands node3 an address with itself as default route
requirements.summary: VyOS DHCP server configured for 10.50.10.0/24 with default-router 10.50.10.254 and committed/saved (cmd-957621a0632c4507). node3 obtained 10.50.10.100/24 via DHCP with default route 10.50.10.254 and pinged the gateway (cmd-78360ba4b8104fcd, cmd-cb3e4116175a46eb). Re-verified after a full reboot of both node1 and node3 (cmd-e8960f3dc07c4a6a, cmd-c42423633a2e433f).

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP on lan-b and hands node4 an address with itself as default route
requirements.summary: Kea DHCPv4 configured with subnet 10.50.20.0/24, routers=10.50.20.254 on opt1/vtnet2 (cmd-a8ae8acc0055402e, cmd-7af14d63efcb4997). A port-67 conflict with a legacy Dnsmasq DHCP scope on vtnet0 was diagnosed via Kea logs (cmd-845716740faf467e) and resolved (cmd-9965f31628474c91, cmd-ad381a5a6ab14fab), after which Kea bound successfully. node4 obtained 10.50.20.100/24 with default route 10.50.20.254 and pinged the gateway (cmd-13be6b9499d54c3c, cmd-73584f5a29d24ff2), reconfirmed after a full reboot of node2 and node4 (cmd-c279fb00ab6e4c20, cmd-47452c6b25ff471c).

requirements.requirement: Static/manual addressing on node3/node4 replaced by DHCP-obtained addressing from the respective per-segment routers
requirements.summary: node3 and node4's NetworkManager-managed second NICs ('Wired connection 2') were reconciled to obtain addresses via DHCP; temporary manual test IPs used during link discovery (192.0.2.x) were removed or superseded by DHCP negotiation, and both nodes ended in a state of dynamic addressing with dynamic default routes confirmed post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes (pre-restart identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: All four nodes show pre-restart boot identity/health, a reboot acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity confirmed independently by the fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot for all four nodes, and recovered DHCP-server/client state with successful gateway pings.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) each serve DHCP on their respective segments, handing node3 and node4 addresses with themselves as default gateway, verified both before and after a full reboot of all four nodes with changed boot identities and recovered DHCP client/server state. The executor also resolved a genuine port-67 conflict on OPNsense caused by a pre-existing Dnsmasq DHCP scope. Hygiene is moderate: most troubleshooting mutations (temporary point-to-point test IPs) were fully reverted, but a few low-risk artifacts were left behind on node2 (unused legacy dhcpd/filter config fragment, un-deleted config.xml backup files).
limitations: Node1's own DHCP lease-table query commands (e.g., 'show dhcp server leases') failed due to shell wrapper issues, so lease-table confirmation relies on interface/route/ping evidence rather than a direct lease list.

No explicit command was observed removing the config.xml.bak-kea/.bak-lanb backup files or the superseded legacy dhcpd/filter config fragment on node2, so their final disposition is inferred rather than directly confirmed absent.
The preparation phase was disabled (prepare_enabled: false) and after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare, so all observed state changes are correctly attributed to the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing exploratory commands were bounded and reverted: temporary point-to-point test addresses used to discover physical link pairing (node1 eth1 cmd-8231868b486d42db, later moved via cmd-d0498cfc688544f9; node3 enp8s0 cmd-2c67c54d222748aa, removed by cmd-8634e282a1724fc0; node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 toggling cmd-b8cbd4a640b8470a/cmd-f410ad8cf6a14fa8, cleared by cmd-c0bf57c6315f4352) left no residue. tcpdump capture files and /tmp/f*.py scratch scripts on node2 were deleted (cmd-278a1186dc4242c8), but that same cleanup did not remove the config.xml.bak-kea and config.xml.bak-lanb backup files it had just listed, leaving stray backup artifacts on node2. An initial legacy 'dhcpd' opt1 section and a manual 'lanb to any' filter rule were added to OPNsense config.xml (cmd-e33727357bc04cf7) before the executor pivoted to configuring Kea for DHCP instead; no command was observed removing this now-superseded, unused fragment. The node4 manual static IP (192.0.2.2/30, cmd-8583d701a2494dce) was not explicitly deleted but was implicitly cleared via later NetworkManager disconnect/reconnect (cmd-bcd7af805e254e2f) before final successful DHCP acquisition. These are low-risk, non-destructive residues rather than damaging or security-weakening changes.
